hook.line: Signs say what is forbidden, and so do cross parents. Spanish has a calm way for rules that belong to nobody and a sharp way for when you personally put your foot down.
hook.es: Está prohibido fumar en el café.
hook.en: Smoking is forbidden in the café.

examples.es: Está prohibido fumar en el café.
examples.en: Smoking is forbidden in the café.
Going in with dogs is forbidden.

examples.es: Está prohibido que los menores entren solos.
examples.en: It is forbidden for minors to go in alone.

examples.es: Está prohibido que Simón hable con los clientes.
examples.en: It is forbidden for Simón to talk to the customers.

examples.es: Te prohíbo que me hables así.
examples.en: I forbid you to speak to me like that. (to a friend)

examples.es: Te prohíbo que salgas esta noche.
examples.en: I forbid you to go out tonight. (to a friend)

rule:
English says "it's forbidden to…" or "I forbid you to…" with the same plain *to* verb. Spanish splits it in two.

For a rule that belongs to nobody, use *está prohibido*. For the bare activity, add an infinitive: *Está prohibido fumar*.

To say who is stopped, add *que* and the changed verb ending: *Está prohibido que los menores entren*. The verb after *que* has its own person and its own ending: *entren*, not *entran*.

When a person forbids another person, use *prohibir* with *te*: *Te prohíbo que me hables así*. It is sharp, a parent or a boss in a bad mood.
smallPrint: Teachers call the changed ending after *que* the present subjunctive. It appears because the sentence is about stopping someone.

readAndPick.es: Está prohibido fumar en el café.
options: Smoking is allowed in the café.
Smoking is forbidden in the café.
You forbid smoking in the café.

readAndPick.es: Te prohíbo que salgas esta noche.
options: I forbid you to go out tonight.
You forbid me to go out tonight.
It is forbidden to go out tonight.

readAndPick.es: Está prohibido que los menores entren solos.
options: Minors forbid anyone to go in alone.
Minors do not need to go in alone.
It is forbidden for minors to go in alone.

readAndPick.es: Te prohíbo que me hables así.
options: You forbid me to speak like that.
I forbid you to speak to me like that.
I forbid myself to speak like that.
Dogs are forbidden to go in alone.
You forbid dogs from coming in.
Going in with dogs is forbidden.

readAndPick.es: Te prohíbo que le des café a Simón.
options: I forbid you to give Simón coffee.
I forbid Simón to give you coffee.
You forbid me to give Simón coffee.

readAndPick.es: Vale me prohíbe que entre a la cocina.
options: I forbid Vale to go into the kitchen.
Vale forbids me to go into the kitchen.
Vale forbids you to go into the kitchen.

readAndPick.es: Está prohibido que Simón hable con los clientes.
options: It is forbidden to talk to Simón.
Simón forbids the customers from talking.
It is forbidden for Simón to talk to the customers.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *fumar* or *fumas*, then type the whole sentence: *Está prohibido ___ en el café.*
yourTurn.answer: Está prohibido fumar en el café.
yourTurn.why: A rule about the bare activity takes the infinitive after *está prohibido*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Going in with dogs is forbidden.
accept: Está prohibido entrar con los perros.
yourTurn.why: No *que* is needed when you only name the activity: *entrar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *entran* or *entren*, then type the whole sentence: *Está prohibido que los menores ___ solos.*
yourTurn.answer: Está prohibido que los menores entren solos.
yourTurn.why: After *que* the verb takes the changed ending, so *entren*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It is forbidden for Simón to talk to the customers.
yourTurn.answer: Está prohibido que Simón hable con los clientes.
yourTurn.why: Naming who is stopped means *que* plus the changed ending: *hable*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I forbid you to go out tonight.
yourTurn.answer: Te prohíbo que salgas esta noche.
accept: Esta noche te prohíbo que salgas.
yourTurn.why: A person forbidding a person uses *te prohíbo que* and the *tú* ending *salgas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it personal. *Está prohibido que me hables así.* Say, to a friend: I forbid you to speak to me like that.
yourTurn.answer: Te prohíbo que me hables así.
yourTurn.why: Swap the rule for *te prohíbo*: now it is you doing the forbidding.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I forbid you to give Simón coffee.
yourTurn.answer: Te prohíbo que le des café a Simón.
yourTurn.why: *Te prohíbo que* is followed by the changed ending, here *des*.

pitfalls.wrong: Está prohibido que fumar en el café.
pitfalls.right: Está prohibido fumar en el café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Que* needs a verb with its own person; for the bare activity, drop *que* and keep the infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Te prohíbo que me hablas así.
pitfalls.right: Te prohíbo que me hables así.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que* the verb takes the changed ending: *hables*, not *hablas*.
Almost. A rule that holds here and now is a state, like *está cerrado*, so it takes *está*.

personal: Write one house rule you would enforce and one you would never. Start with *Está prohibido…* for the rule, and *Te prohíbo que…* for the order.
